claim_boundary: Self-reported learning progress is not verified evidence, certification or runtime acceptance.

tracks.reader: Understand the vessel — no Docker required
tracks.builder: Commission the software lab — Docker-capable Linux host
tracks.investigator: Reconstruct an incident — commissioned lab or reviewed evidence

modules.title: Define the lab's promise and limits
modules.objective: Separate simulated process, real software protocol and marine reference claims.
modules.practice: Make a three-column scope map. Place Cargo physics, Modbus TCP and ship-shore ESD in the correct columns.
modules.evidence: A scope map with one limitation per layer; no runtime evidence needed.
modules.explain: Why does a realistic dashboard not prove a working controller?
modules.checkpoint: I can name what is implemented and what the lab cannot prove without looking at notes.

modules.title: Read the vessel as a connected system
modules.objective: Trace cargo electrical demand through PMS and machinery dependencies.
modules.practice: Annotate one official vessel-system figure: source, pump, electrical supply, operator and safety boundary.
modules.evidence: An attributed figure reference and a written Cargo → PMS → machinery trace.
modules.explain: Which consequences of losing power would you expect before seeing any packets?
modules.checkpoint: I can explain one cross-domain dependency and distinguish it from a safety-system claim.

modules.title: Separate command, feedback and consequence
modules.objective: Distinguish an output command, equipment feedback and a measured process result.
modules.practice: Predict pump behavior when the start request is true but valve-open feedback is false. Trace the actual permissive in CargoControl.st.
modules.evidence: A command/feedback/process table with the PLC symbol and its I/O-map row.
modules.explain: Why can pump feedback be true while measured flow is zero?
modules.checkpoint: I can trace a permissive and explain why command success is not process success.

modules.title: Trace the real paths through the lab
modules.objective: Separate the Modbus control conduit, OPC UA supervision and coordinator process APIs.
modules.practice: Trace Cargo flow from its equation to I/O, PLC, publication and evidence. Mark every clock and every protocol change.
modules.evidence: A source-linked trace using the generated I/O map and the architecture contract.
modules.explain: Why must a coordinator API change not be described as a Modbus write?
modules.checkpoint: I can identify where a packet capture can and cannot establish causality.

modules.title: Commission without confusing health with readiness
modules.objective: Produce a commit-bound commissioning run and stop honestly at manual gates.
modules.practice: On an isolated Linux host, run setup, review and commission start. Keep the printed run path. Commission the PLCs and discover live NodeIds before binding.
modules.evidence: A real commissioning directory and retained Gate A–E observations; never fabricated PASS files.
modules.explain: What is the difference between a running container and a commissioned signal?
modules.checkpoint: I can explain my first blocked gate and the exact evidence needed to move forward.

modules.title: Explain cargo behavior with physics
modules.objective: Distinguish blockage, pump failure and sensor bias using independent process evidence.
modules.practice: Read the worked blocked-flow case. On a commissioned lab, record a normal baseline before a controlled blocked-flow experiment. Predict the consequence first.
modules.evidence: A normal-versus-fault explanation; live investigators also retain PCAP, state and alarm timelines.
modules.explain: What evidence would falsify your blockage explanation?
modules.checkpoint: I can separate a physical contradiction from a suspicious network event.

modules.title: Read a message all the way to meaning
modules.objective: Map a Modbus message to its address, engineering unit and consequence; explain OPC UA quality and clocks.
modules.practice: Follow the packet-lab example, then annotate a different captured transaction without its walkthrough. Never infer authorization from port number alone.
modules.evidence: A decoded message, matching I/O-map entry, and expected-conduit classification.
modules.explain: Can a valid Modbus packet still represent an unsafe or unauthorized action?
modules.checkpoint: I can explain the request, source, address, scaling and process meaning of one transaction.

modules.title: Reason from alarms to operator decisions
modules.objective: Distinguish FUXA operator alarms, the Teaching Alarm Chronicle and certified safety systems.
modules.practice: Rationalize one alarm: trigger, persistence, consequence, operator response, clear and acknowledgement. Compare the actual chronology after a controlled fault.
modules.evidence: An alarm-response card; live builders also retain HMI screenshots and commissioned FUXA export.
modules.explain: Why does acknowledging an alarm not remove its cause?
modules.checkpoint: I can explain the operator response and name the alarm source without conflating systems.

modules.title: Keep navigation claims inside the evidence
modules.objective: Distinguish recorded NMEA 0183 replay from a live GNSS receiver and optional CAN references.
modules.practice: Annotate one recorded sentence and its timestamp provenance. List what the replay cannot prove about vessel position, authenticity or NMEA 2000 compatibility.
modules.evidence: A replay provenance note and a parsed sentence; label every replay artifact.
modules.explain: Why does a plausible position not establish trustworthy navigation data?
modules.checkpoint: I can state the replay and licensing boundaries without claiming marine conformance.

modules.title: Defend a cross-layer incident reconstruction
modules.objective: Compare network-only, process-only and cross-layer explanations with falsifiable conclusions.
modules.practice: Complete the investigation capstone. Reveal the layers in stages, revise the hypothesis, and have another reader score the final explanation.
modules.evidence: A scored case report with source paths, hashes, clock limitations, alternative explanations and verified experiment indexes.
modules.explain: Which conclusion changed when process evidence was revealed, and which remains unknown?
modules.checkpoint: I can defend a causal sequence and a limitation without calling an unmeasured benefit proven.
